note: MISSING-DIAGNOSTIC issue: the reported symptom is a CLEAN COMPILE, so exit 0 is the bug and a failed compile can be the FIX. The predicate is therefore anchored positively rather than being a bare absence test. Clause 1 is the positive anchor: the out-of-bounds element `indices[3]` reaches codegen as `i32 undef` in the index operand of the StructuredBuffer load for `g_vertices[indices[3]].normal` (repro.hlsl line 124 col 118). It proves three things at once -- the compile got past Sema, DXIL was emitted, and the out-of-bounds read was silently accepted. `\w*[Bb]ufferLoad` matches both `dx.op.rawBufferLoad.f32` (what lib_6_6 emits) and `dx.op.bufferLoad.f32` (what the compute translation emits), so the same predicate scores both. Clause 2 is the absence clause and is what a fix would break: any diagnostic naming the index as out of range -- error OR warning, which is what the reporter asked for -- makes the predicate no-match. It deliberately does NOT test for the word `warning` alone, because `-Zi` without an output file always emits `warning: no output provided for debug - embedding PDB in shader container`, which has nothing to do with this issue. Absence clauses are satisfied for free by a compile that never started (SKILL.md step 4); clause 1 is what prevents that here -- a release that rejects `lib_6_6` emits no buffer load either, so it scores no-repro and is then demoted to invalid-probe by the feature-absence marker rather than counted as a reproduction. KNOWN OVERLAP: clause 2 also matches the DXIL validator's `Access to out-of-bounds memory is disallowed`, which is not a front-end diagnostic. That never fires on the primary repro (no probed release emits it there), but it does fire on the compute translation under v1.4.1907, where the same source is rejected late by the validator instead -- see variant-compute-v1.4.1907.txt. Clause 1 fails there anyway, so nothing turns on the overlap; it is recorded so the next reader does not read `no-match` on that capture as 'v1.4.1907 diagnosed the index'. CONTROLS, both --expect no-match, both captured: control-diagnosed.hlsl is the identical shader with the same access hoisted into a local (`const uint oob = indices[3];`), which DXC DOES diagnose -- it proves clause 2 fires when a diagnostic is present, and that the predicate is not merely 'this compiled'. control-inbounds.hlsl is the identical shader with `indices[3]` changed to `indices[2]`, a correct program that compiles clean -- it proves clause 1 discriminates and that the predicate is not satisfied by every successful compile.
